verses.en: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;
verses.pt: Depois da morte de Saul, tendo Davi voltado da derrota dos amalequitas e estando há dois dias em Ziclague,
verses.en_web: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had stayed two days in Ziklag;
verses.en_bbe: Now after the death of Saul, when David, having come back from the destruction of the Amalekites, had been in Ziklag for two days;

verses.en: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
verses.pt: ao terceiro dia veio um homem do arraial de Saul, com as vestes rasgadas e a cabeça coberta de terra; e, chegando ele a Davi, prostrou-se em terra e lhe fez reverência.
verses.en_web: on the third day, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul, with his clothes torn, and earth on his head. When he came to David, he fell to the earth, and showed respect.
verses.en_bbe: On the third day a man came from Saul's tents, with his clothing out of order and earth on his head: and when he came to David, he went down on the earth and gave him honour.

verses.en: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.
verses.pt: Perguntou-lhe Davi: Donde vens? Ele lhe respondeu: Escapei do arraial de Israel.
verses.en_web: David said to him, “Where do you come from?” He said to him, “I have escaped out of the camp of Israel.”
verses.en_bbe: And David said to him, Where have you come from? And he said, I have come in flight from the tents of Israel.

verses.en: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
verses.pt: Davi ainda lhe indagou: Como foi lá isso? Dize-mo. Ao que ele lhe respondeu: O povo fugiu da batalha, e muitos do povo caíram, e morreram; também Saul e Jônatas, seu filho, foram mortos.
verses.en_web: David said to him, “How did it go? Please tell me.” He answered, “The people have fled from the battle, and many of the people also have fallen and are dead. Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.”
verses.en_bbe: And David said to him, How did things go? Give me the news. And in answer he said, The people have gone in flight from the fight, and a great number of them are dead; and Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.

verses.en: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?
verses.pt: Perguntou Davi ao mancebo que lhe trazia as novas: Como sabes que Saul e Jônatas, seu filho, são mortos?
verses.en_web: David said to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?”
verses.en_bbe: And David said to the young man who gave him the news, Why are you certain that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?

verses.en: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
verses.pt: Então disse o mancebo que lhe dava a notícia: Achava-me por acaso no monte Gilbea, e eis que Saul se encostava sobre a sua lança; os carros e os cavaleiros apertavam com ele.
verses.en_web: The young man who told him said, “As I happened by chance on Mount Gilboa, behold, Saul was leaning on his spear; and behold, the chariots and the horsemen followed close behind him.
verses.en_bbe: And the young man said, I came by chance to Mount Gilboa, and I saw Saul supporting himself on his spear; and the war-carriages and horsemen overtook him.

verses.en: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I.
verses.pt: Nisso, olhando ele para trás, viu-me e me chamou; e eu disse: Eis-me aqui.
verses.en_web: When he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. I answered, ‘Here I am.’
verses.en_bbe: And looking back, he saw me and gave a cry to me. And answering him I said, Here am I.

verses.en: And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
verses.pt: Ao que ele me perguntou: Quem és tu? E eu lhe respondi: Sou amalequita.
verses.en_web: He said to me, ‘Who are you?’ I answered him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
verses.en_bbe: And he said to me, Who are you? And I said, I am an Amalekite.

verses.en: And he said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me.
verses.pt: Então ele me disse: Chega-te a mim, e mata-me, porque uma vertigem se apoderou de mim, e toda a minha vida está ainda em mim.
verses.en_web: He said to me, ‘Please stand beside me, and kill me; for anguish has taken hold of me, because my life lingers in me.’
verses.en_bbe: Then he said to me, Come here to my side, and put me to death, for the pain of death has me in its grip but my life is still strong in me.

verses.en: So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.
verses.pt: Cheguei-me, pois, a ele, e o matei, porque bem sabia eu que ele não viveria depois de ter caído; e tomei a coroa que ele tinha na cabeça, e o bracelete que trazia no braço, e os trouxe aqui a meu senhor.
verses.en_web: So I stood beside him and killed him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he had fallen. I took the crown that was on his head and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them here to my lord.”
verses.en_bbe: So I put my foot on him and gave him his death-blow, because I was certain that he would not go on living after his fall: and I took the crown from his head and the band from his arm, and I have them here for my lord.

verses.en: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:
verses.pt: Então pegou Davi nas suas vestes e as rasgou; e assim fizeram também todos os homens que estavam com ele;
verses.en_web: Then David took hold on his clothes, and tore them; and all the men who were with him did likewise.
verses.en_bbe: Then David gave way to bitter grief, and so did all the men who were with him:

verses.en: And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.
verses.pt: e prantearam, e choraram, e jejuaram até a tarde por Saul, e por Jônatas, seu filho, e pelo povo do Senhor, e pela casa de Israel, porque tinham caída à espada.
verses.en_web: They mourned, wept, and fasted until evening, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Yahweh, and for the house of Israel; because they had fallen by the sword.
verses.en_bbe: And till evening they gave themselves to sorrow and weeping, and took no food, weeping for Saul and for Jonathan, his son, and for the people of the Lord and for the men of Israel; because they had come to their end by the sword.

verses.en: And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.
verses.pt: Perguntou então Davi ao mancebo que lhe trouxera a nova: Donde és tu? Respondeu ele: Sou filho de um peregrino amalequita.
verses.en_web: David said to the young man who told him, “Where are you from?” He answered, “I am the son of a foreigner, an Amalekite.”
verses.en_bbe: And David said to the young man who had given him the news, Where do you come from? And he said, I am the son of a man from a strange land; I am an Amalekite.

verses.en: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the LORD’S anointed?
verses.pt: Davi ainda lhe perguntou: Como não temeste estender a mão para matares o ungido do Senhor?
verses.en_web: David said to him, “Why were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy Yahweh’s anointed?”
verses.en_bbe: And David said to him, Had you no fear of stretching out your hand to put to death the one marked with the holy oil?

verses.en: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.
verses.pt: Então Davi, chamando um dos mancebos, disse-lhe: chega-te, e lança-te sobre ele. E o mancebo o feriu, de sorte que morreu.
verses.en_web: David called one of the young men, and said, “Go near, and cut him down!” He struck him so that he died.
verses.en_bbe: And David sent for one of his young men and said, Go near and put an end to him. And he put him to death.

verses.en: And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the LORD’S anointed.
verses.pt: Pois Davi lhe dissera: O teu sangue seja sobre a tua cabeça, porque a tua própria boca testificou contra ti, dizendo: Eu matei o ungido do Senhor.
verses.en_web: David said to him, “Your blood be on your head; for your mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I have slain Yahweh’s anointed.’”
verses.en_bbe: And David said to him, May your blood be on your head; for your mouth has given witness against you, saying, I have put to death the man marked with the holy oil.

verses.en: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:
verses.pt: Lamentou Davi a Saul e a Jônatas, seu filho, com esta lamentação,
verses.en_web: David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son
verses.en_bbe: Then David made this song of grief for Saul and Jonathan, his son:

verses.en: (Also he bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jasher.)
verses.pt: mandando que fosse ensinada aos filhos de Judá; eis que está escrita no livro de Jasar:
verses.en_web: (and he commanded them to teach the children of Judah the song of the bow; behold, it is written in the book of Jashar):
verses.en_bbe: (It is recorded in the book of Jashar for teaching to the sons of Judah) and he said:

verses.en: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!
verses.pt: Tua glória, ó Israel, foi morta sobre os teus altos! Como caíram os valorosos!
verses.en_web: “Your glory, Israel, was slain on your high places! How the mighty have fallen!
verses.en_bbe: The glory, O Israel, is dead on your high places! How have the great ones been made low!

verses.en: Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
verses.pt: Não o noticieis em Gate, nem o publiqueis nas ruas de Asquelom; para que não se alegrem as filhas dos filisteus, para que não exultem as filhas dos incircuncisos.
verses.en_web: Don’t tell it in Gath. Don’t publish it in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
verses.en_bbe: Give no news of it in Gath, let it not be said in the streets of Ashkelon; or the daughters of the Philistines will be glad, the daughters of men without circumcision will be uplifted in joy.

verses.en: Ye mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew, neither let there be rain, upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, as though he had not been anointed with oil.
verses.pt: Vós, montes de Gilboa, nem orvalho, nem chuva caia sobre, vós, ó campos de morte; pois ali desprezivelmente foi arrojado o escudo dos valorosos, o escudo de Saul, ungido com óleo.
verses.en_web: You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain on you, and no fields of offerings; For there the shield of the mighty was defiled and cast away, The shield of Saul was not anointed with oil.
verses.en_bbe: O mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain on you, you fields of death: for there the arms of the strong have been shamed, the arms of Saul, as if he had not been marked with the holy oil.

verses.en: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.
verses.pt: Do sangue dos feridos, da gordura dos valorosos, nunca recuou o arco de Jônatas, nem voltou vazia a espada de Saul.
verses.en_web: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, Jonathan’s bow didn’t turn back. Saul’s sword didn’t return empty.
verses.en_bbe: From the blood of the dead, from the fat of the strong, the bow of Jonathan was not turned back, the sword of Saul did not come back unused.

verses.en: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
verses.pt: Saul e Jônatas, tão queridos e amáveis na sua vida, também na sua morte não se separaram; eram mais ligeiros do que as águias, mais fortes do que os leões.
verses.en_web: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives. In their death, they were not divided. They were swifter than eagles. They were stronger than lions.
verses.en_bbe: Saul and Jonathan were loved and pleasing; in their lives and in their death they were not parted; they went more quickly than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

verses.en: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with other delights, who put on ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
verses.pt: Vós, filhas de Israel, chorai por Saul, que vos vestia deliciosamente de escarlata, que vos punha sobre os vestidos adornos de ouro.
verses.en_web: You daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you delicately in scarlet, who put ornaments of gold on your clothing.
verses.en_bbe: O daughters of Israel, have sorrow for Saul, by whom you were delicately clothed in robes of red, with ornaments of gold on your dresses.

verses.en: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, thou wast slain in thine high places.
verses.pt: Como caíram os valorosos no meio da peleja!
verses.en_web: How the mighty have fallen in the middle of the battle! Jonathan was slain on your high places.
verses.en_bbe: How have the great ones been made low in the fight! Jonathan is dead on your high places.

verses.en: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
verses.pt: Angustiado estou por ti, meu irmão Jônatas; muito querido me eras! Maravilhoso me era o teu amor, ultrapassando o amor de mulheres.
verses.en_web: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan. You have been very pleasant to me. Your love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
verses.en_bbe: I am full of grief for you, my brother Jonathan: very dear have you been to me: your love for me was a wonder, greater than the love of women.

verses.en: How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!
verses.pt: Como caíram os valorosos, e pereceram as armas de guerra!
verses.en_web: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!”
verses.en_bbe: How have the great ones been made low, and the arms of war broken!
